subject: Request: SLA carve-outs, credit caps, and onboarding exception - Greenline Analytics
messages:
From: Sara Patel <sara@greenline-analytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, procurement@greenline-analytics.com
Cc: Tom Huang <thomas.huang@greenline-analytics.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: SLA template questions + request for carve-outs

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the product walkthrough last week — the team is excited to move forward. Before legal and procurement sign off on the SOW, our procurement team has a couple of asks on the SLA template we wanted to surface:

- Uptime baseline: Greenline's internal mandates prefer a 99.90% minimum during our initial ramp (first 3–6 months) to account for integration tests and staged traffic. Can Redwood offer a temporary onboarding floor for the first quarter?
- Scheduled maintenance: we'd like planned maintenance windows (up to 4 hours/month) to be excluded from uptime calculations for the first 6 months while we coordinate the bulk ingestion windows.
- Monthly credit cap: we need a hard cap on service credits so our Finance team can model maximum exposure — proposing a cap of 30% of monthly recurring fees.
- Latency: we also have a soft requirement that p95 generation latency should stay below 500ms for our 2k-token batch profiles; can you confirm whether latency commitments can be added to the SLA or at least captured in the runbook?

I've attached the SOW draft so you can see our timelines and traffic ramp plan. Please let me know what compromises you can make — we're aiming to finalize commercial terms this month.

Thanks,
Sara Patel
Head of Platform Procurement
Greenline Analytics
Attachment: greenline_sow_draft.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara@greenline-analytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SLA template questions + request for carve-outs

Hi Sara — really appreciate the clarity and timeline in the SOW. Quick responses to each ask and a proposal for compromise: 

- Onboarding uptime floor: Redwood's standard hosted SLA is 99.95% and Dedicated is 99.99%. For new customers with a documented ramp plan, we can offer a temporary floor of 99.90% for the first 90 days (not 6 months) as an onboarding exception — provided we have the canary schedule and traffic migration dates in the SOW.
- Scheduled maintenance carveout: we can agree to exclude up to 2 hours/month of scheduled maintenance from uptime calculations for the first 180 days. Anything beyond that would need to be scheduled with 72 hours' notice and mutually agreed windows.
- Monthly credit cap: Redwood normally caps credits at one monthly recurring fee. Given Greenline's ask, we're willing to state an explicit cap of 30% of monthly recurring fees for the first 6 months, after which the standard cap (100% of monthly fees) resumes.
- Latency: we can include service-level objectives for latency as non-financial SLOs in the runbook. Operationally we can commit to p95 generation latency < 500ms for the 2k-token profile on Dedicated capacity; for hosted, we'll commit to a p95 < 750ms and provide a latency dashboard for monthly review. If you require financial remedy tied to latency, we need to scope that separately with Product/Legal.

I've drafted a marked-up SLA (redwood_sla_draft_v2.pdf) and an uptime calculation sheet that shows how the carveouts affect monthly calculations. See attachments. Our commercial ask: acceptance of a 90-day 99.90% onboarding floor + the 2-hour carveout for the first six months. If acceptable, we'll circulate a countersign-ready SOW and routing to Legal/Finance.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Manager, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood_sla_draft_v2.pdf; uptime_calculation_sheet.xlsx
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 11:06:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: SLA template questions + request for carve-outs

Looping Legal and Pricing: forwarding Greenline's asks and Marissa's proposed compromises. A few internal notes / suggested edits before we send the countersign: 

- Credit bands: instead of sliding percentages by 0.1% increments, propose three discrete bands for simplicity and auditability: >=99.95% (no credit), 99.50%–99.95% (10% monthly credit), <99.50% (25% monthly credit). Cap overall credits at one month's fee after the initial six-month exception window.
- Emergency maintenance carveout: require at least 24 hours notice for any non-security emergency maintenance, and specify that security-driven interruptions (e.g., zero-day mitigation) are not eligible for credits.
- Onboarding exception: tolerate the 90-day 99.90% floor for the first project with Greenline only; include a clause that the exception is void if Greenline initiates more than two full cluster resizes or changes to planned architecture during the onboarding window.

I'll draft the changes and send to Legal and Laura for redlines. If we agree, Marissa — can you ask Greenline to confirm the PO timing so Finance can model the 30% cap request for the first 6 months?

-Ben
Director, Commercial Ops
From: Sara Patel <sara@greenline-analytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Huang <thomas.huang@greenline-analytics.com>, procurement@greenline-analytics.com
Date: Fri, 4 Dec 2026 10:33:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SLA template questions + request for carve-outs

Marissa / Ben — thanks for the quick turnaround and for being flexible. Greenline is generally comfortable with the 90-day 99.90% onboarding floor and the 2-hour scheduled maintenance carveout for the first 6 months, provided we get two things in writing: 

1) A description of the canary plan and fallback policy (how you will route to a previous model/instance) so our SREs can coordinate; please add that to the runbook appendix.
2) The 30% credit cap for months 1–6 documented explicitly in the SLA. After month 6 we'll revert to Redwood's standard cap.

We have initiated the PO internally and aim to route it next week. I've attached the PO template to the procurement mailbox and signed the SOW in DocuSign; link included below.

Thanks,
Sara
Attachment: PO_template_greenline.pdf
Related link: https://www.docusign.com/sign/ABC-GL-058
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara@greenline-analytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Dec 2026 11:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SLA template questions + request for carve-outs

Sara — great, appreciate the quick confirmation. Next steps: 

- I'll have Legal and Laura finalize the redline incorporating the three-band credit structure Ben suggested, the 90-day onboarding floor, and the explicit 30% cap for months 1–6. Expect an updated countersign package by EOD tomorrow.
- Karthik will add the canary/fallback description to the runbook appendix (non-binding SLO language for hosted vs Dedicated).
- Please route the PO to finance@redwood.com and paste my address so I can confirm receipt. Once PO is in hand and DocuSign is complete, we'll flip the countersign and schedule the kickoff call.

If anything else comes up from Greenline Legal, loop me directly and mark the subject with [SLA].

Best,
Marissa
Senior Sales Manager, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood_sla_draft_v2.pdf (pending final redlines)
